newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds rally to end week on stronger note.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds rally to end week on stronger note.

text.p: Canadian bonds rallied on Friday to end a strong week higher as the market extended its recent gains, analysts said.
"Just an extension of very positive market tone," said Toronto-Dominion Securities Inc analyst Arve Benkisrud. "There's no real news."
Sheldon Dong, manager of fixed-income research at Midland Walwyn, added some reluctant investors capitulated and threw their cash into the market after missing earlier rallies.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.63 to C$117.14 to yield 6.670 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 8/32 to yield 6.66 percent. The negative spread between the two bonds narrowed to one basis point from three at Thursday's close.
This week's slew of economic news trickled to a near halt on Friday.
A raft of buyers are sending bond prices higher, Dong added. "We've found very few sellers at these levels." "They're holding long bonds for long-term positions."
Market players will keep one eye on this weekend's Group of Seven leading industrial nations, whose leaders could discuss foreign currency exchanges, analysts said.
Dong added that the bond market, which is already venturing into uncharted territory, could rally further on a technical basis.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.25 to C$198.55 to yield 6.077 percent, compared to its U.S. equivalent which rose 3/32 to yield 6.38 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 30 basis points from 26 basis points at Thursday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 2.80 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.07 percent.
